title: MYP eAssessment Results: When and How to Check
summary: MYP eAssessment results are released on fixed IB dates. Learn when results arrive, how schools share them, and what to do after opening yours.
body_markdown:
For an MYP student, results day often begins with a refresh button. A hypothetical student opens the school portal, checks their inbox, closes both, and tries again three minutes later. Their parent watches from a tactful distance, unsure whether to ask a question or make tea.


The useful answer is simpler than the waiting makes it feel. **MYP eAssessment results** for the May session are issued from 12:00 noon GMT on 1 August. Results for the November session are issued from 12:00 noon GMT on 1 February of the following year. The IB makes results available to schools through IBIS, and students should follow the access instructions provided by their MYP coordinator or school.


Not every school communicates results in the same way. Some may use an online school portal, while others may send a report or arrange collection. Your coordinator is therefore the best source for the exact time and method that apply to you.


### MYP eAssessment results at a glance


Question Short answer


When are May-session results issued? From 12:00 noon GMT on 1 August


When are November-session results issued? From 12:00 noon GMT on 1 February of the following year


Where does the school receive them? Through the IB Information System, known as IBIS


How does a student see them? Through the process chosen and communicated by their school


Who helps with missing or unexpected results? The school’s MYP coordinator


Can a result be reviewed? The school can discuss available enquiries upon results with the student and family


These dates come from the IB’s current[MYP registration and results schedule](https://www.ibo.org/programmes/middle-years-programme/assessment-and-exams/onscreen-examinations/registration/) . Because the stated release time is in GMT, families should convert it carefully to their local time zone rather than assuming noon locally.


A student repeatedly refreshes a laptop while a parent asks whether they are checking the school email


*Results-day nerves are not always about the website.*


### How to access your MYP eAssessment results


The most important distinction is between the system used by the IB and the route used by the student. The IB releases results to authorized schools through IBIS. That does not necessarily mean every student receives a personal IBIS login.


A sensible access process looks like this:


- Read any results-day instructions sent by your school.
- Confirm whether results will appear in a school portal, arrive by email, or be distributed another way.
- Keep your candidate information available if your coordinator has asked for it.
- Check the release time in your own time zone.
- Contact the MYP coordinator if information is missing or inaccessible.
- Avoid repeatedly guessing passwords, since this can create a second problem on an already stressful day.


Students taking particular subjects can also read RevisionDojo’s guides to[accessing MYP English Language and Literature results](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/accessing-myp-english-language-literature-eassessment-results) and[accessing MYP Standard Mathematics results](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/accessing-myp-standard-mathematics-eassessment-results) . The basic principle is the same: the school coordinates access and remains the first point of contact.


If no message has arrived before results day, ask the school in advance. A five-minute conversation with the coordinator is worth far more than an hour spent searching for a portal your school does not use.


### What appears in an MYP results report?


MYP eAssessment is not identical to every classroom assessment completed during the IB Middle Years Programme. It is an optional, internationally moderated assessment model for eligible students in the final year of the programme. Schools choose how they participate and which students or components they register.


Depending on the registration, eAssessment can involve on-screen examinations, externally marked or moderated ePortfolios, the personal project and interdisciplinary learning. A student’s report should therefore be read in the context of the components for which that student was actually registered.


MYP subject results use the familiar 1-7 grade scale. That final grade should not be confused with the raw marks or criterion totals students may have seen during classroom assessment. RevisionDojo’s guide to[MYP assessment criteria by subject](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-criteria-per-subject) explains how criterion-based classroom assessment works, while its overview of[MYP English Language and Literature assessment](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-english-language-literature-assessment) explores one subject in greater depth.


This distinction matters because a result can feel surprising even when it is not inexplicable. Classroom tasks, external components and on-screen examinations do not all measure performance in precisely the same setting. One reflects work completed across a course; another may capture performance under a defined assessment format.


### How parents can make results day easier


Parents often want to interpret the number immediately. Students often need a moment before interpretation begins. Both instincts are understandable, but timing matters.


Start by checking that the report is complete and belongs to the correct session. Then allow the student to react. A result can carry relief, pride, disappointment and uncertainty at the same time. Turning the first minute into a strategic meeting rarely improves the conversation.


Once emotions have settled, ask practical questions:


- Does the report include every component the student expected?
- Is there a grade that differs sharply from school feedback?
- Does the school recommend a follow-up conversation?
- Could the outcome affect progression or future subject choices?
- Is there a deadline for any results-related service?


The MYP is designed as a broad programme, so one grade should be interpreted as part of a wider academic picture. Students exploring where their strengths may lead can review the[MYP subjects covered by RevisionDojo](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-myp-subjects-covered) or consider how[MYP subjects can complement English Language and Literature](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/subjects-that-pair-with-myp-english-language-and-literature) .


### What to do if a result looks wrong


First, distinguish disappointment from a possible administrative or assessment issue. A grade below the student’s hope is not, by itself, evidence of an error. But a missing component, inaccessible report or result that seems inconsistent with the information held by the school deserves a calm question.


Contact the MYP coordinator and identify the exact subject or component involved. Ask the coordinator to explain the result and the options available through the IB. The official schedule states that enquiries upon results begin on the day results are issued.


The school should explain the relevant procedure, deadline, fee and possible outcomes before anything is requested. Families should also ask whether a reviewed result could remain unchanged or move in either direction. Do not rely on social media instructions or assume that another school’s process applies to yours.


Keep copies of the report and relevant school correspondence. A short, specific message usually works best: name the component, explain the concern and ask what formal options are available.


### Turning the result into a useful next step


A result is a measurement taken at one point. It matters, but it is not a complete biography of the student who receives it.


If the outcome is strong, identify what produced it. Perhaps the student practised unfamiliar questions, understood the criteria or learned to manage time. If the outcome is disappointing, diagnose before increasing the workload. More revision is not automatically better revision.


RevisionDojo is built to support that diagnosis across the IB journey. Students can use the **Questionbank** and **Mock Exams** for targeted practice, then turn weak areas into a plan with **Study Notes** , **Flashcards** and **AI Chat** . **Grading tools** can make feedback more immediate, while **Predicted Papers** help students rehearse demanding assessment conditions. For longer-term support, the **Coursework Library** and experienced **Tutors** can help students connect criteria with concrete improvements.


A student preparing to strengthen literary analysis, for example, can move from the result to a focused guide on[how to score a 7 in MYP Language and Literature](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-score-a-7-in-myp-language-and-literature) . That is the healthier arc of results day: receive the number, understand what it means, and decide what to do next.


### The calmest way to approach results day


Know the official date, follow the school’s instructions and keep the coordinator’s contact details nearby. When the result arrives, check it before interpreting it. When interpretation begins, focus on patterns rather than panic.


The refresh button feels powerful because waiting offers so little control. The real control comes afterward. With clear explanations, subject-specific resources and RevisionDojo’s complete MYP and IB toolkit, a result can become something more useful than a verdict. It can become a direction.
